feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
This is a strong, credible CV with clear senior-level positioning in digital communications, especially for mission-driven or public-sector organizations. It reads polished and substantive, but it would be more impactful with tighter structure, fewer repeated themes, and more quantified outcomes beyond platform scale.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear professional brand: the headline, summary, and experience consistently position you as a digital strategy and communications leader.  
- Strong credibility: long progression at NACo shows advancement, increasing responsibility, and domain depth in web, email, social, analytics, and multimedia.  
- Good writing quality overall: language is professional, concise, and largely error-free, with no obvious misspellings.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these sections would improve scannability and free space for achievements.  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more outcome metrics would strengthen impact, e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, campaign performance, or adoption improvements.  
- Fix minor style/grammar inconsistencies: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; standardize serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “content operations and enterprise web improvement”); and keep punctuation/bullet formatting consistent, especially the dash-led bullets embedded in paragraphs.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more distinctive opening, tighter phrasing, and a bit less overlap with the competencies and experience sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for grammar and cleaner style.
- Lead with current senior value proposition: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven organizations.
- Trim channel lists slightly and emphasize outcomes or scope rather than repeating skills listed elsewhere.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that enable effective communications at scale. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and “stakeholder coordination” closely overlap with Core Competencies and Soft Skills.
- Detailed channel/platform references are repeated extensively in Work Experience and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize higher-level strengths rather than repeating detailed skill categories listed elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Shift from broad/generic phrases to sharper, senior-level capabilities: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “CMS modernization,” “Editorial governance,” “Analytics & insight reporting.”
- Standardize style and parallel structure; use either all noun phrases or all “X & Y” constructions.
- Replace weaker wording like “Multi-channel communication” with “Cross-channel communications leadership” or “Integrated communications strategy.”
- Consider a tighter version: Enterprise digital strategy • CMS modernization & web operations • Editorial governance & workflow design • Cross-channel communications leadership • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Systems architecture & process improvement • Stakeholder alignment & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and the header.
- “Web & CMS administration,” “Data analytics & reporting,” and “Multimedia & live event production” repeat Topline Skills/Technical sections.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the phrasing and foreground outcomes, scale, and the most distinctive work so it adds to—not repeats—your NACo entries.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client type: “Embedded consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, and communications operations modernization.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one stronger line: “Built cross-channel workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/campaign bullet more outcome-led: “Designed and launched modular Drupal campaign experiences, including microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Split out the standout technical item: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content requirements, and discovery UX.” Add metrics if possible: users served, pages improved, time saved, launch status.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance,” “analytics,” and “organization-wide communications” strongly overlap with the Director of Digital Media role.
- The microsite/AI search work also appears in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad first sentence with an outcome-led summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Consolidate bullets and lead with the biggest win: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more results-based: add audience growth, engagement, email performance, production volume, or cost/time savings if available; otherwise shorten.
- Tighten the rest to action + outcome: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio…” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve leadership visibility and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo bullets; emphasize building the studio/capability, not recurring production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about operational leadership, editorial systems, and channel growth at the manager-to-director transition point.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and progression: “Directed day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy messaging.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and distinct: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems bullet: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” overlap with the Director role’s “governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.”
- “weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; keep this version focused on scaling/operationalizing, not initial creation.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it largely repeats the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize leadership scope and strategic outcomes rather than generic communications phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive bullets:
- Enterprise digital strategy and web modernization
- Editorial governance and content operations at scale
- Cross-channel communications leadership for complex organizations
- Public-sector advocacy storytelling and audience strategy
- Swap “messaging” for “storytelling” or “communications strategy” to sound more senior and less tactical.
- Replace “audience-focused content planning” with “content operations at scale” or “audience strategy” for stronger executive positioning.
- If space allows, align wording with recent impact: “web modernization,” “governance,” and “operations” reflect the strongest 2022–present work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps heavily with multiple NACo experience bullets; keep this section broader and more distinctive.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution strengths, not repeat every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages)”
- Prioritize recent, differentiating strengths: “CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation”
- Keep only standout systems that support your recent work: “Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages) • CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “jQuery” feels dated and low-value given your seniority; cut unless required for target roles.
- Most platform/tool names already appear in “Technical + IT”; avoid mirroring that section too closely.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making value and outcomes, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics infrastructure & performance insights: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Replace generic terms with sharper business language: “KPI framework development” instead of “KPI design,” and “executive dashboarding” instead of “leadership reporting.”
- Add one optimization lens if accurate: “SEO, UX behavior analysis, and conversion/performance optimization.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics infrastructure & optimization — GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity; KPI framework development, executive dashboarding, SEO, UX behavior analysis, and performance optimization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills higher-level and let Technical + IT hold the full tool list.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and older NACo experience. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, more current capabilities and tools rather than generic production terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, senior-level wording: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “PTZ camera and studio systems,” “Virtual event operations.”
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event production workflows”
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier tied to recent work: “Built and operated in-house studio workflows for advocacy and event programming.”
- Keep only 3–4 items; “video production and editing” + “studio operations” can be combined to reduce listiness.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section duplicates “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies; use one or make this version more tool/workflow-specific.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with “Livestreaming”; combine them.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. In a recent, impact-led CV, this section should either add specificity or be trimmed.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show level/relevance, e.g. “Drupal (primary enterprise CMS) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, prioritize by recency/use: put Drupal first and consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a notable project.
- Consider adding brief qualifiers only where meaningful: “Drupal 9/10,” “SharePoint Online,” or “Power Pages (Microsoft ecosystem)” if accurate.
- Keep this item strictly platform-focused; avoid mixing in modernization or implementation language already covered elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” under Topline Skills; consider deleting one version or making this one more concise.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles and projects, so avoid overemphasizing it in multiple sections.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and tools most relevant to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Rewrite as: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If space allows, add light qualifiers tied to recent work: Front-end development for Drupal-based sites • API integrations • tag management • edge/serverless scripting • deployment automation
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used consistently elsewhere; “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner and more senior

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills: “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations,” and “Workflow automation.” Keep this section tool-focused and let Topline Skills carry broader capability language.
- “GitHub Actions” may fit better under “Automation & Workflow Systems” unless you want this item strictly scoped to implementation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems
- Reorder by relevance/strength: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp
- If space allows, add light grouping for clarity: Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/workflow: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams
- Best upgrade: replace pure list format with capability framing, e.g. “Workflow automation and team operations: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Trello, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Basecamp”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Slack” and “Teams” are common workplace tools; unless central to systems design, they add less value than automation/build tools.
- This item duplicates adjacent skills sections; keep it concise and let recent roles demonstrate impact.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses a chance to signal scale or level of ownership. It should also align more clearly with the strong email leadership already shown in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform naming for readability: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add level/context in brief: Enterprise email campaign management • newsletter operations • audience segmentation
- Best rewrite: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp | Enterprise email campaigns, newsletter operations, audience segmentation

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and NACo email/newsletter bullets, so avoid adding generic claims like “email marketing” without a differentiator.
- Don’t overstate CRM ownership unless you directly managed segmentation, journeys, or platform administration.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, site refresh support, and multimedia production.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and contribution: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh size/timeline, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or workflow improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped standardize day-to-day digital production workflows.”
- Clarify supervision modestly: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate on daily production and publishing.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthening workflows” overlaps with the 2018–2022 and 2022–2024 NACo entries; keep this version tactical, not governance-heavy.
- “Weekly video updates” appears in the next role; distinguish this item by framing it as launch/early production.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or scope, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize the standout achievement first: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer action: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audiences served, cross-team partners, or types of projects supported.
- Keep this entry lighter than later NACo roles since web, video, and digital operations are covered more strongly in 2015–2024 positions.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media entries; keep this focused on innovation/research support and the podcast launch.
- Avoid repeating video, livestream, or editorial workflow language already used in 2015–2024 roles.
